subject: science
passage: The southern cassowary, a large flightless bird of the rainforests of northern Australia and New Guinea, eats mainly fruit that has fallen to the forest floor. It swallows the fruit whole, and the seeds pass through its body undamaged. Because the bird walks long distances each day, it drops those seeds far from the parent tree. For some rainforest plants with very large fruit, the cassowary is the only animal big enough to spread their seeds at all.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To describe the diets of the flightless birds of Australia
choices.B: To describe how far the cassowary walks in a single day
choices.C: To argue that the cassowary is the most important animal in the rainforest
choices.D: To explain the role the cassowary plays in spreading rainforest seeds

explanation.why: Every sentence points in the same direction: the cassowary eats fruit, the seeds "pass through its body undamaged," it carries them "far from the parent tree," and for some plants it is "the only animal big enough to spread their seeds." The text explains the bird's role as a seed spreader.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Only one bird is discussed; the text never describes other flightless birds or their diets.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The bird's long walks are mentioned only to explain why seeds end up far from the parent tree; they are a detail, not the main point.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The text says the cassowary is the only seed spreader for some large-fruited plants, not that it is the most important animal overall.
explanation.D: Correct. The text explains how the cassowary's eating and walking habits carry seeds away from parent trees, and why that matters for some plants.
